l: Every member of the Department should participate in good grooming practices that will create and maintain a highly respectable image for themselves, their fellow members, and the police profession. The following appearance standards noted in sections A, B, C, and D shall apply to all commissioned personnel, Traffic Control Technicians, Civilian Response Specialists, and Police Trainees. The appearance standards shall be strictly adhered to, unless the Chief of Police has granted a written exception.

Hairstyles worn by personnel shall be neat, clean, present a well-groomed conservative and professional appearance. Hair color shall be of conservative tone and will not distract from a professional appearance and will be limited to colors that are natural or conservative artificial variations. Exceptions shall be permitted at the discretion of a division captain and while the employee is on active undercover or vice control assignment.
B. Mustaches, Sideburns, Beards, and Goatees - Non-Uniformed and Uniformed TBP 2.13

a. If a mustache is worn, it shall be neatly trimmed off the lips and not extend more than ¼” below the corners of the mouth. Extreme styles such as handlebar mustaches, excessively bushy, rolled, or curled styles are prohibited.

a. If an individual desires to wear sideburns, they shall be neatly trimmed and tapered. Sideburns may extend to the lowest part of the earlobe and shall end in a clean-shaven horizontal line. Sideburns shall not be flared or any wider at the bottom than their natural width at the top.

a. If a natural beard or full set is worn, it shall be worn with a mustache and cover the complete jaw line. Cheeks shall be shaved on and above the lower edge of the cheekbone. The neck shall be shaven on and below the Adam’s apple.

a. The goatee will be described as a mustache that extends down around the side of the mouth and joins hair on the chin, also referred to as a circle beard. If an individual desires to wear a goatee, it shall be worn with a mustache and the cheeks, jaw line, and neck will remain clean shaven.

5. The facial hair policy is not intended for individuals who forget to shave prior to their shift and attempt to use provisions in this policy as reasons to sporadically stay in compliance. Employees choosing to grow facial hair shall begin the growth during time off and may not report for duty with less than two (2) day’s growth, provided that such time is sufficient to present an intentional and established growth. The following styles of facial hair are NOT permitted:
a. Chin Strap Beards – Beards that are trimmed to a thin line along the jaw.
b. Patchy Beards – Beards of uneven or patchy growth. (excluding those resulting from scars)
c. Beards Taking Excessive Time to Grow – If, after two (2) weeks of growth, the beard remains patchy.
d. Designer Stubble – Beards shorter than 1/16 of an inch.
e. Neck beards – Beards with all areas shaved above the jawline leaving the beard only on the neck.
6. All facial hair shall conform to the following restrictions:
a. The bulk of the beard (distance that the mass of facial hair protrudes from the skin of the face) shall not exceed ½ of an inch;
b. No portion of the beard shall be exceptionally longer than the rest;
c. No designs may be shaved into facial hair; no braids, bow, or other objects are allowed in facial hair;
d. Facial hair must be neatly sculpted and trimmed at all times;
e. Officers shall not claim a constant state of growth, only to avoid shaving on a regular basis; and,
f. Facial hair must be natural in color and cannot be intentionally colored to contrast the hair on the scalp.

g. Per the Occupational Health and Safety Administration (OSHA) Respiratory Standard, respirators shall not be worn when facial hair comes between the sealing surface of the face piece and the face, or that interferes with valve function. Employees electing to maintain a beard shall shave the portion of their face that comes into contact with the respirator seal when mobilized or any time the use of a respirator is likely.
h. During instances where a Class A uniform has to be worn for a funeral or special event, the Chief of Police or designee may require officers to be clean shaven.

The department recognizes that employees may have a medical need to have facial hair which is outside of policy. A reason for this includes, but is not limited to, Pseudofolliculitis Barbae or types of skin cancer.

1. Exemptions shall be case-by-case and require a medical waiver issued by a licensed medical provider, approved by an Assistant Chief, and filed with the Medical Records Custodian (MRC) in Police Employment Services.
a. Exemptions expire one (1) year from the date of approval and the officer must re-apply. Medical Records Custodians shall review and monitor the waiver.
2. If the waiver is approved, facial hair will be kept trimmed and neat, not to exceed ¼” in length. “Chin strap” and designer beards are strictly prohibited.
3. If the officer shaves his facial hair after receiving a waiver, the waiver will become void and the officer will have to submit another waiver request for facial hair.
1. Hair must be neat, professional, and present a groomed appearance.
2. Officers’ hairstyles shall be maintained so as to not hinder the safety of the officer nor compromise the ability to perform the requirements and duties as an officer of the Department.

3. Officers shall wear their hair in styles that do not interfere with the proper wearing or alter the original shape of uniform headgear. Hair shall not protrude onto the forehead below the band of the properly worn headgear.

4. Hairstyles shall not feature styles that incorporate shaved emblems, symbols, and/or names; tails; Mohawks; faux hawks; pigtails; or any other styles that distract from the professional appearance of officers.
5. Hair color shall be of a natural or artificial variant of a natural color.
6. Hair shall be arranged so as not to interfere with vision in any way. Bangs must be kept above the brow line.
7. Braiding, twisting, and locking hairstyles are permitted if the hairstyle conforms to all other uniform standards.
8. Hairpieces including extensions and wigs, are acceptable if they meet the prescribed requirements for hairstyles.
9. Officers, if in uniform, shall arrange their hair so it does not extend past the bottom edge of the shirt collar at the center of the back when worn down.

a. Hair that extends below the bottom edge of the shirt collar shall be pulled back in the form of a ponytail, braid, or bun. All ponytails, buns, and braids will be grouped to the back of the head and centered as best as possible. The grooming and style must be maintained under all but the most adverse conditions.
b. Hair that is pulled back in braids or a single ponytail cannot extend beyond the yoke line of the uniform shirt at the center of the back and must be professional in appearance.
NOTE: The yoke line refers to the horizontal hem on the uniform shirt that runs across the shoulder blades.

c. Hairpins, barrettes, hair clips, hair bands, and headbands should be black, dark blue, or closely match the hair color so as not to be conspicuous. Items used by officers to hold the hair in place shall be concealed as much as possible. Headbands, if worn, shall be no more than one (1) inch wide and cannot have visible lettering, emblems, or brands. Decorative items, such as ribbons or beads, shall not be worn in the hair.

d. Employees may request religious exemptions (i.e., hair length, head covers, and other items of religious significance) from the Chief of Police. The Chief of Police, or designee, shall determine on a case-by-case basis considering any potential safety issues and operational concerns.

Hairstyles for non-sworn personnel shall be professional in appearance and not feature unkempt styles. Hair color shall be of conservative tone and will not distract from a professional appearance and will be limited to colors that are natural or conservative artificial variations. Mustaches, sideburns, beards, and goatees are permitted for non-sworn personnel and shall follow the standards listed above for sworn personnel.
1. Ensure employees conform to standards set forth in this General Order.

2. Approve whether facial hair and grooming standards are in compliance with this General Order. A supervisor’s decision regarding an employee’s non-conformance to the standards set forth herein is not subject to the grievance process; however, an employee can appeal to the next supervisor in their chain of command if there is a disagreement.
1. First time offense will require the officer to conform with the policy prior to starting their shift.
2. More than one (1) violation within a six (6) month period will require the officer to remain clean shaven for the following three (3) months.
